title: knee, leg and ankle (round the whole limb)

chart.description: The knee, leg and ankle unrolled round the whole limb. u: distance round the limb (cm) from the anterior midline (patellar ligament, tibial crest, front of the ankle), positive towards lateral (round the fibular side), negative towards medial (round the tibial side). The back of the limb is reached round the LATERAL side: the posterior midline (the middle of the popliteal crease, the groove between the heads of gastrocnemius, the calcaneal tendon) lies at about u = +18.5 at the knee, narrowing to +16 at mid-calf and +11 at the ankle as the limb tapers; the posteromedial knee and calf (the semitendinosus tendon, the medial border of the calcaneal tendon) are reached round the medial side (u = -10 to -13). Below the malleoli the chart continues down the sides of the heel towards the sole. v: distance along the limb (cm) from the inferior pole of the patella (knee flexed), positive cranial (towards the thigh), negative towards the ankle and heel. d: depth below the skin (cm). Offsets keep the chart's sense: 'lateral' is further round the fibular side (behind the fibula, over the calf) and 'medial' further round the tibial side (behind the tibia).

configurations.label: knee flexed (seated, or supine with a bolster under the knee)

landmarks.label: inferior pole (apex) of the patella
landmarks.palpation: Follow the patella down to its lower tip.

landmarks.label: midpoint of the superior border (base) of the patella
landmarks.palpation: The upper border of the patella, at its middle.

landmarks.label: medial end of the base of the patella
depression lateral to the patellar ligament (lateral knee eye)
landmarks.palpation: With the knee flexed, the hollow lateral to the patellar ligament, below the patella. Shallower with the knee straight.

landmarks.label: depression medial to the patellar ligament (medial knee eye)
landmarks.palpation: With the knee flexed, the hollow medial to the patellar ligament.

landmarks.label: tibial tuberosity
landmarks.palpation: The bony prominence where the patellar ligament inserts.

landmarks.label: head of the fibula
landmarks.palpation: The rounded bony knob on the outer side of the leg below the knee.

landmarks.label: depression below the medial condyle of the tibia, at the medial border of the tibia
landmarks.palpation: Slide up the medial border of the tibia until the finger stops under the condyle.

landmarks.label: centre of the front of the ankle joint (between extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus tendons)
landmarks.palpation: Dorsiflex the foot: the hollow between the two tendons at the ankle crease.

landmarks.label: prominence of the lateral malleolus
prominence of the medial malleolus
midpoint of the popliteal crease
landmarks.palpation: Prone, the knee slightly flexed: the middle of the transverse crease at the back of the knee.

landmarks.label: lateral end of the popliteal crease, at the medial border of the biceps femoris tendon
landmarks.palpation: Flex the knee against resistance: the biceps femoris tendon stands out at the outer side of the back of the knee; the crease ends at its medial border.

landmarks.label: medial end of the popliteal crease, at the lateral border of the semitendinosus tendon
landmarks.palpation: Flex the knee against resistance: the semitendinosus tendon is the most prominent cord at the inner side of the back of the knee; the crease ends at its lateral border.

landmarks.label: depression at the medial end of the popliteal crease, anterior to the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons
landmarks.palpation: With the knee flexed, the hollow between the back of the medial femoral condyle and the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons.

landmarks.label: lateral epicondyle of the femur
landmarks.palpation: The most prominent point on the outer side of the lower femur, above the joint line.

landmarks.label: depression above and behind the lateral epicondyle of the femur, between the iliotibial band and the biceps femoris tendon
landmarks.palpation: Flex the knee: above and behind the lateral femoral epicondyle, the hollow between the iliotibial band in front and the biceps femoris tendon behind.

landmarks.label: apex of the angle where the two bellies of gastrocnemius join the calcaneal tendon
landmarks.palpation: Prone: ask the patient to press the toes down against resistance; the two bellies of gastrocnemius stand out and form an inverted V over the calcaneal tendon, about halfway between the popliteal crease and the heel.

landmarks.label: inferior border of the lateral head of gastrocnemius where it meets the calcaneal tendon
landmarks.palpation: With the calf contracted, the lower edge of the outer belly of gastrocnemius, about 1 B-cun lateral and inferior to the apex of the inverted V (about 7 B-cun above BL60).

landmarks.label: medial border of the calcaneal tendon, level with the prominence of the medial malleolus
landmarks.palpation: Pinch the calcaneal tendon behind the ankle: its inner edge, level with the tip of the bulge of the medial malleolus.

landmarks.label: lateral border of the calcaneal tendon, level with the prominence of the lateral malleolus
landmarks.palpation: Pinch the calcaneal tendon behind the ankle: its outer edge, level with the bulge of the lateral malleolus.

landmarks.label: tibialis anterior tendon at the ankle crease
landmarks.palpation: Dorsiflex and invert the foot: the thick tendon on the inner side of the front of the ankle.

landmarks.label: inferior tip of the lateral malleolus
landmarks.palpation: Follow the lateral malleolus down to its lower end.

landmarks.label: depression anterior and inferior to the lateral malleolus, lateral to the extensor digitorum longus tendon (opening of the sinus tarsi)
landmarks.palpation: Invert the foot slightly: the soft hollow in front of and below the lateral malleolus, lateral to the tendons to the toes.

landmarks.label: tuberosity of the navicular
landmarks.palpation: The bony knob on the inner border of the foot, in front of and below the medial malleolus.

landmarks.label: the sole directly below the prominence of the medial malleolus
landmarks.palpation: The plantar surface of the heel vertically below the medial malleolus (with the foot flat).

landmarks.label: border of the red and white skin on the lateral side of the calcaneus, directly below the hollow between the lateral malleolus and the calcaneal tendon
landmarks.palpation: On the outer side of the heel, follow the line down from the hollow behind the lateral malleolus to where the dorsal skin meets the plantar skin.

segments.label: knee (level of the lateral knee eye) to the prominence of the lateral malleolus

description: The anterior knee and leg. The patellar ligament runs from the inferior pole of the patella to the tibial tuberosity, with the 'knee eye' depressions either side of it; deep to them lie the infrapatellar fat pad and then the knee joint cavity. The anteromedial surface of the tibia is subcutaneous. Lateral to the tibial crest lies tibialis anterior; deep to it, on the interosseous membrane, run the anterior tibial vessels with the deep fibular nerve. The common fibular nerve winds round the neck of the fibula just below and behind the fibular head. Medially the great saphenous vein ascends in front of the medial malleolus and along the medial leg; behind the tibia lie the posterior tibial vessels and the tibial nerve. Behind the knee the popliteal fossa, bounded by the biceps femoris tendon laterally and the semitendinosus and semimembranosus tendons medially, holds in its fat, from superficial to deep, the tibial nerve, the popliteal vein and the popliteal artery, which lies on the back of the joint capsule; the common fibular nerve follows the medial border of the biceps femoris tendon to the neck of the fibula. In the calf the two heads of gastrocnemius join the calcaneal tendon about halfway down; soleus lies deep to them, and deeper still the tibial nerve and the posterior tibial vessels. The small saphenous vein and the sural nerve run up from behind the lateral malleolus to the middle of the calf. Behind the medial malleolus the flexor retinaculum covers the tendons of tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus, the posterior tibial artery, the tibial nerve and flexor hallucis longus; between both malleoli and the calcaneal tendon lies the pre-Achilles fat. In front of the ankle the joint capsule lies beneath the extensor tendons; the great saphenous vein passes in front of the medial malleolus.

review.notes: Positions and depths are illustrative approximations of a reference adult written for simulation. They are not measurements or an atlas and are not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.
